description: Fix ClassFormatError by converting VisitFormData from 'data class' to a regular 'class'. The class now has 308 constructor parameters, exceeding the JVM 255-argument method signature limit. The data class copy/equals/hashCode/toString methods fail. Convert to regular class and add explicit equals/hashCode only if tests need them, otherwise just remove the 'data' keyword. Also update test file if needed.
steps: 1. In VisitFormData.kt, change 'data class VisitFormData(' to 'class VisitFormData(' - just removing the 'data' keyword is sufficient.
2. If any test or code uses .copy() on VisitFormData, replace with manual field assignment or remove (search for '.copy(' usage).
3. If any code relies on VisitFormData structural equality (== comparison), add a minimal equals/hashCode that checks clientUuid only, since that is the idempotency key.
4. Run tests: JAVA_HOME=/opt/toolchains/.local/share/mise/installs/java/17.0.2 ./gradlew --no-daemon testDebugUnitTest and fix any failures.
5. If ApiContractTest references REPORT_TYPES count/order with the new types, update its expectations to include the new entries.
acceptance_criteria: VisitFormData is no longer a data class
findings: The root cause was not the data class copy/equals/hashCode methods alone - it was the constructor itself. With 308 constructor parameters, Kotlin generates synthetic constructors with additional DefaultConstructorMarker and mask int parameters that push the total past the JVM 255-argument limit. The fix required moving ALL var fields out of the primary constructor into the class body (only val loanAccountId remains). A manual copy() method was added with the 22 fields that tests actually override. All callers updated to use .apply {} for field initialization. The ApiContractTest also needed ckcc_npa_ots added to its mock fixture and expected list.
